titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Birth of Nebuchadnezzar (ch. 76, part 2 of 2)
part: ch. 76, part 2 of 2 — The Birth of Nebuchadnezzar
about: Karmin, warned by the angel, flees with gold and sends his family to Jerusalem while he goes to Babylon, where King Belaon welcomes him and lodges him near the house of an absent merchant (?). The merchant's wife takes Karmin as a lover and bears his child; the king's wife bears a wingless bird-like creature. The two maids, meeting by God's will, swap the infants, and Karmin's son grows up as Nebuchadnezzar, who takes Jerusalem, raises a golden statue, is driven out for his pride and restored, and the kingdom of Babylon stays with his line.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ተንሥአ ፡ ሶቤሃ ፡ ወኀሠሠ ፡ ወርቀ ፡ አስከሬን ፡ ወነሥኣ ፡ ወአንቅሃ ፡ ለብእሲቱ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ክልኤ ፡ ደቂቁ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ አንቅሀ ፡ አግብርቲሁ ፡ እለ ፡ ኀረየ ፡ ወአጾሮሙ ፡ ንዋየ ፡ ክብር ፤
sentences.l: And-then he-arose at-once, and-he-sought gold ʾaskaren (?), and-he-took-it, and-he-woke-her to-his-wife with two his-sons, and-again he-woke his-servants who he-chose, and-he-made-them-carry goods-of glory;
sentences.i: Then he rose at once and sought out gold (?), and took it; he woke his wife and his two sons, and woke again the servants whom he had chosen, and had them carry costly goods;
sentences.n: The subject is Karmin, who has just fled by night on the angel's warning (end of part 1); the verbs are 3rd-masculine-singular perfects with no stated subject. Reading the verbs: ወ- 'and' is prefixed to almost every verb in this narrative (ወኀሠሠ, ወነሥኣ, ወአንቅሃ), so most units open with ወ-; I will not repeat that. ተንሥአ is the tä-stem of ነሥአ ('rise'); ወነሥኣ 'and he took it' carries the object suffix -ኣ (a feminine 'it', gold being treated as feminine). ወርቀ is the accusative of ወርቅ 'gold'. አስከሬን after it is a word I cannot read with confidence (?): it may be a qualifier of the gold or a foreign or corrupt word, so the translation just says 'gold (?)'. (From memory, Amharic አስከሬን means 'corpse'; a Geʿez reading 'the gold of the corpse' is not one I can support (?).) አንቅሃ / አንቅሀ is the causative (ʾa-stem) of ነቅሀ 'be awake', so 'make awake, wake'; ወአንቅሃ (with ሃ, fourth order) is 3ms perfect + the object suffix -ኣ 'her', doubled by ለብእሲቱ, whereas the second አንቅሀ, 'woke again', takes a stated object (አግብርቲሁ) and has no suffix. ለብእሲቱ: the ለ- marks the object and the suffix -ቱ is 'his' (ብእሲት + -ሁ), so 'his wife'. ደቂቁ 'his sons' is the plural ደቂቅ + -u. አጾሮሙ is the causative of ጾረ 'carry a load' (root ṣ-w-r): 'he made them carry'. ንዋየ ክብር is a construct chain 'goods-of glory', i.e. costly, honourable goods. This is the first of many units that end in the clause-marker ፤ (a mid-sentence break) rather than ።.

sentences.t: ወወፅአ ፡ በሌሊት ፡ ወፈነዎሙ ፡ ለብእሲቱ ፡ ወለደቂቁ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ክልኤ ፡ አግብርቲሁ ፡ ይባኡ ፡ ኢየሩሳሌም ፤
sentences.l: And-he-went-out by-night, and-he-sent-them, to-his-wife and-to-his-sons, with two his-servants, that-they-enter Jerusalem;
sentences.i: And he went out by night and sent his wife and his sons, with two of his servants, to go into Jerusalem;
sentences.n: ወፈነዎሙ 'and he sent them': ፈነወ 'send' + -ዎሙ 'them'. The people sent are named after the verb with the object-marking ለ- (ለብእሲቱ ወለደቂቁ 'his wife and his sons'), an anticipating pattern: the pronoun suffix on the verb is repeated by a ለ-noun; flagged here, and I will only nudge it later. ይባኡ is the 3rd-plural subjunctive of ቦአ 'enter' (the root b-w-ʾ), so 'that they may enter'; it takes ኢየሩሳሌም directly as a place accusative with no preposition. Jerusalem is the home city of the Israelites in this story; Karmin sends his family there, while he goes the other way to Babylon.

sentences.t: ወውእቱሰ ፡ ሖረ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ክልኤ ፡ አግብርቲሁ ፡ ርሑቀ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ መጠነ ፡ ምሕዋረ ፡ ፫ ፡ አውራኅ ፡ ወበጽሐ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ባቢሎን ፡ ወቦአ ፡ ኀበ ፡ በላዖን ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ባቢሎን ፡ ወአብአ ፡ አምኃ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወነገሮ ፡ ዘከመ ፡ መጽአ ፡ ኀቤሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-for-his-part he-went with two his-servants far land as-far-as journey-of 3 months, and-he-reached land-of Babylon, and-he-entered to Belaon king-of Babylon, and-he-brought-in gifts to-him, and-he-told-him how he-came to-him;
sentences.i: As for him, he went with his two servants to a land far away, a journey of three months, and reached the land of Babylon. He went in to Belaon, king of Babylon, brought him gifts, and told him how he had come to him;
sentences.n: ወውእቱሰ 'and he, for his part': the pronoun ውእቱ + the contrastive enclitic -ሰ, which sets this person against the one just mentioned (the family going to Jerusalem). That enclitic recurs all through this part (ወይእቲሰ, ወነጋዲሁሰ, ወራብዖሙሰ) and is rendered 'as for X'. ሖረ 'he went' (ሖረ, root ḥ-w-r). ርሑቀ ብሔረ 'far, a land': ርሑቅ 'far' is in the accusative as an adverb, then ብሔረ 'a land' (accusative of the goal; it could also be the construct 'land of' with መጠነ ... as its dependent, 'a land of the extent of a three-month journey' (?)); መጠነ 'as far as, to the extent of' is a construct and takes ምሕዋረ 'a journey-of' ፫ አውራኅ. ፫ is the numeral 3 (spoken ሠለስቱ śälästu), and ወርኅ 'month' has the plural አውራኅ. Numerals are kept as written throughout. በላዖን 'Belaon' is the name of the king of Babylon here (Geʿez form kept in l, Belaon in i); ንጉሠ ባቢሎን 'king-of Babylon' is a construct chain. ወአብአ is the causative of ቦአ (ወቦአ 'and he entered' just before), so 'he brought in'; አምኃ 'gifts'. ሎቱ = ለ + -ቱ 'to him'. ዘከመ 'how' (lit. 'that-as'). መጽአ ኀቤሁ: 'he came to him', with the preposition ኀበ + -hu.

sentences.t: ወአፍቀሮ ፡ ለባኦን ፡ ለካርሚን ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ማኅደረ ፡ በአግዋረ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ነጋዲሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-loved-him to-Baʾon to-Karmin, and-he-gave-him lodging in-neighbourhood-of (?) house-of his-merchant;
sentences.i: And Baʾon (apparently the king) loved Karmin and gave him lodging near the house of his merchant (?);
sentences.n: The grammar here is irregular (?). ወአፍቀሮ is 'and he loved him' (አፍቀረ + -ኦ), and both names carry the object/dative ለ-: ለባኦን ለካርሚን. The spellings ባኦን and ካርሚን also differ from በላዖን and ከርሚን elsewhere. I read ባኦን as the king (Belaon, the same Babylonian king) with a loose spelling, and Karmin as the one he loved; the other reading, that Karmin loved Baʾon, is possible given the doubled ለ-. ወወሀቦ 'and he gave him' (ወሀበ + -ኦ). ማኅደረ 'a lodging' (accusative). አግዋረ I cannot identify with certainty (?): I take it as 'neighbourhood, vicinity' (from the idea of 'neighbour'), so 'in the neighbourhood of the house', with ቤተ the construct of ቤት 'house', 'house-of'. ነጋዲሁ is ነጋዲ 'merchant' + -hu 'his': the king's merchant (?), who is introduced here and is away; he becomes the husband in the next units.

sentences.t: ወነጋዲሁሰ ፡ ሖረ ፡ ርሑቀ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ መጠነ ፡ ፫ ፡ ዓመት ፡ ወለእሉሰ ፡ እለ ፡ ሐሰዉ ፡ ስምዐ ፡ ቀተልዎሙ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ምስካብ ፡ በቤት ፨
sentences.l: And-his-merchant-for-his-part he-went far land as-far-as 3 year, and-for-those-for-their-part who they-lied witness, they-killed-them in-the bed in-the house;
sentences.i: As for his merchant, he had gone to a far country for three years; and as for those who had borne false witness, they were killed in the bed in the house.
sentences.n: Two ሰ-contrasts in one sentence (see the note on the third unit). መጠነ ፫ ዓመት 'as much as 3 years', i.e. 'for three years': the numeral ፫ is followed by the singular ዓመት 'year', (unlike ፫ አውራኅ, plural, in the third unit, so the number agreement is loose; the spoken form with the feminine ዓመት would be ሠለስ (?), not the ሠለስቱ of አውራኅ). ሐሰዉ is the 3rd-plural perfect of ሐሰወ 'lie, speak falsely', and ስምዐ is the accusative of ስምዕ 'testimony', so 'they lied a testimony', i.e. 'bore false witness': these are the two false witnesses of part 1. ቀተልዎሙ 'they killed them' (ቀተለ 'kill' + -ዎሙ). The subject of 'they killed' is not stated; presumably the king's men sent after Karmin, who found the witnesses in the house instead (?); the text says only 'in the bed in the house'. ምስካብ 'bed, place of lying down'. This unit ends at ፨, a larger break marker, though the sentence stops short of a full stop.

sentences.t: ወአፍቀረቶ ፡ ለከርሚን ፡ ብእሲተ ፡ ነጋዲ ፡ ወተስሕተት ፡ ቦቱ ፡ ወፀንሰትእስመ ፡ እኩይ ፡ ምግባሪሆን ፡ ለአንስት ።
sentences.l: And-she-loved-him to-Karmin wife-of merchant, and-she-erred with-him and-she-conceived-for evil deeds-their to-women.
sentences.i: And the merchant's wife loved Karmin, and went astray with him, and conceived. For the deeds of women are evil.
sentences.n: ወፀንሰትእስመ in the text is two words run together, ወፀንሰት 'and she conceived' (ፀንሰ, 3fs perfect) and እስመ 'for, because'; I have split it. The subject ብእሲተ ነጋዲ 'wife-of merchant' (a construct chain) comes after the verb, as the word order is verb first: ወአፍቀረቶ 'and she loved him' (the suffix -ቶ 'him') is repeated by ለከርሚን, the anticipating-object pattern noted above. ወተስሕተት 'and she erred' is the tä-stem of ሰሕተ; the sense is 'went astray, sinned', here adultery. ቦቱ 'with him' (በ + -ቱ). ምግባሪሆን 'their deeds' (ምግባር + -ሆን, 3fp); ለአንስት 'of/for women' (አንስት, the plural of ብእሲት 'woman'). The last clause is the narrator's own aside, in the general voice of this chronicle's moral comments on women; I render it plainly and do not soften it.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ኀደጋ ፡ ብእሲሃ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ፅንስት ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ወወለደት ፡ ወወሀበት ፡ ለሐፃኒት ፡ ወአልሀቀት ፤
sentences.l: For he-left-her her-husband while pregnant she, and-she-bore, and-she-gave to-nurse, and-she-brought-up;
sentences.i: For her husband had left her while she was pregnant, and she bore the child, gave it to a nurse, and had it raised;
sentences.n: እስመ 'for, because', then ኀደጋ 'he left her' (ኀደገ + -ኣ). ብእሲሃ 'her husband' (ብእሲ 'man, husband' + -ሃ 'her'). እንዘ 'while' + ፅንስት ይእቲ 'she (is) pregnant', a circumstantial clause with a nominal predicate. ወወለደት 'and she bore', ወወሀበት 'and she gave' (3fs perfects). ለሐፃኒት 'to a nurse' (ሐፃኒት, feminine of ሐፃኒ). ወአልሀቀት is the causative (ʾa-stem) of ልህቀ 'grow', so 'she made (it) grow, brought up'; whether the nurse or the mother is the subject is not clear (?), and the rendering 'had it raised' covers both. The child is male by implication of the later references.

sentences.t: ወበካልእ ፡ ዓመት ፡ ተስሕተት ፡ ወፀንሰት ፡ እምኀበ ፡ ከርሚን ፡ እስመ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ላሕዩ ፡ ለከርሚን ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ በውስተ ፡ እስራኤል ።
sentences.l: And-in-other year she-erred and-she-conceived from Karmin, because good his-appearance to-Karmin exceedingly in-midst Israel.
sentences.i: And in the next year she went astray again and conceived by Karmin, for Karmin's appearance was exceedingly handsome among the Israelites.
sentences.n: ካልእ 'other, second' (በካልእ ዓመት 'in the second/next year'). ተስሕተት and ፀንሰት as above. እምኀበ ከርሚን 'from Karmin' (እም- 'from' + ኀበ 'at the side of'). እስመ ሠናይ ላሕዩ ለከርሚን: ሠናይ 'good, fine'; ላሕዩ 'his appearance' (ላሕይ + -u); the ለ- on ለከርሚን marks the possessor, a common way to say 'Karmin's appearance' ('his appearance, Karmin's'). ፈድፋደ 'exceedingly'. በውስተ እስራኤል 'among Israel' (ውስተ 'in the midst of'). The explanation is the narrator's: she desired the Israelite for his looks.

sentences.t: ወይእቲሰ ፡ ፈቀደት ፡ ለዘፀንሰቶ ፡ ወሊዳ ፡ ትግድፎ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ባሕር ፡ ወትጽንሖ ፡ ለነጋዲ ፡ ብእሲሃ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘኢተስሕተት ፡ ወኢገብረት ፡ ምንተኒ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-for-her-part she-wished, for-what she-had-conceived when-having-borne-it, she-might-cast-it into sea, and-she-might-wait-for-him to-merchant her-husband as one-who-not she-had-erred and-not she-had-done anything;
sentences.i: But she wished, when she had given birth to what she had conceived, to cast it into the sea and to wait for her husband the merchant as one who had not gone astray and had done nothing;
sentences.n: ወይእቲሰ 'and she, for her part': ይእቲ + -ሰ. ለዘፀንሰቶ ወሊዳ is a heavy phrase: ለ- (object marker) + ዘ 'that which' + ፀንሰቶ 'she conceived it', followed by ወሊዳ, a gerund 'having borne' (the feminine gerund ending -a). ትግድፎ 'she might throw it out' (3fs subjunctive of ገደፈ 'cast away', + -ኦ). ወትጽንሖ is 'and she might wait for him' (ጸንሐ 'wait, remain', 3fs subjunctive + -ኦ), the suffix doubled by ለነጋዲ ብእሲሃ 'the merchant, her husband' (object with ለ-). ከመ ዘኢተስሕተት 'like one who had not erred': ዘ + ኢ- 'not'. ወኢገብረት ምንተኒ 'and had not done anything': ምንት 'what' + the enclitic -ኒ gives 'anything' after a negative.

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ጠቢብ ፡ ፫ ፡ የዐጽበኒ ፡ በኅሊናየ ፡ ወራብዖሙሰ ፡ ስእንኩ ፡ ጠይቆቶ ፡ አሠረ ፡ ንስር ፡ በውስተ ፡ ሰማይ ፡ ወፍኖተ ፡ አርዌ ፡ ምድር ፡ በዲበ ፡ ኰኵሕ ፡ ወፍኖተ ፡ ሐመር ፡ በዲበ ፡ ባሕር ፤
sentences.l: As said Solomon the-wise, 3 are-hard-for-me in-my-mind, and-the-fourth-of-them as-for, I-was-unable examining-it: trace-of eagle in-midst sky, and-way-of beast-of earth upon rock, and-way-of ship upon sea;
sentences.i: As Solomon the wise said: 'Three things are hard for me in my mind, and the fourth I have been unable to examine: the track of an eagle in the sky, and the way of a beast of the earth upon a rock, and the way of a ship upon the sea;
sentences.n: Allusion: Proverbs 30:18-19, ascribed to Solomon ('Three things are too wonderful for me, four I do not understand: the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a serpent on a rock, the way of a ship on the high seas, and the way of a man with a young woman'). The Geʿez keeps the eagle, the creature on the rock and the ship, and then, in the next unit, replaces the fourth thing with the faithless wife. በከመ ይቤ 'as he said' (በ- + ከመ 'in the way that'; ይቤ 'he said'); ሰሎሞን ጠቢብ 'Solomon the wise'. ፫ 'three' as a numeral. የዐጽበኒ: ዐጸበ 'be hard, be troublesome', 3ms imperfect + -ኒ 'to me'; I read it as 'is hard for me' (?); the Hebrew behind Proverbs 30:18 has 'too wonderful for me', and ዕጹብ 'marvellous' may be from the same root, so 'marvellous' is possible (?). ራብዖሙ 'the fourth of them' (ራብዕ 'fourth' + -ሙ 'them'), with the enclitic -ሰ. ስእንኩ 'I was unable' (1cs perfect of ስእነ); ጠይቆቶ 'to examine it' (infinitive ጠይቆት + -ኦ 'it', as in ወሊዶታ below). አሠረ 'track, trace, footprint' (construct, from አሠር); ፍኖተ 'way-of' (construct of ፍኖት); አርዌ ምድር 'beast-of earth' (አርዌ is 'wild beast' and, I believe, also 'serpent' (?), so the Geʿez may well intend the serpent of the Hebrew; I render the words as they stand); ሐመር 'ship'; በዲበ 'upon'. Geʿez has no quotation marks; I mark the speech with them for English.

sentences.t: ወራብዖሙሰ ፡ ስእንኩ ፡ ጠይቆ ፡ ዘይቤ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ብእሲት ፡ እኪት ፡ እንተ ፡ ትዔምፅ ፡ ምታ ፡ ወተኀፂባ ፡ ትነብር ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘኢገብረት ፡ ወትምሕል ፡ እንዘ ፡ ትሔሱ ፨
sentences.l: And-the-fourth-of-them as-for, I-was-unable to-examine, that-which he-said concerning woman evil who she-wrongs her-husband, and-having-washed she-sits as one-who not she-did, and-she-swears while she-lies.
sentences.i: And the fourth I have been unable to examine is what he said about the wicked woman who wrongs her husband, and, having washed, sits as one who has done nothing, and swears while she lies.'
sentences.n: ዘይቤ 'that which he said' (ዘ- + ይቤ). በእንተ 'concerning' takes a following word without the construct change here (ብእሲት እኪት 'woman evil'; እኪት is the feminine of እኩይ 'evil'). እንተ 'who' (feminine relative). ትዔምፅ 'she wrongs' (ዐመጸ 'act wrongly, do injustice', 3fs imperfect) + ምታ 'her husband' (ምት 'husband' + -ሃ 'her'). ተኀፂባ 'having washed' (feminine gerund of ተኀፅበ); ጠይቆ 'to examine' is by shape the masculine gerund, used as the complement of ስእንኩ (?). ትነብር 'she sits, dwells'. ወትምሕል 'and she swears' (3fs imperfect; the shape fits a G-stem ምሕለ rather than ማሐለ, but the citation form I cannot fix without Dillmann (?)). እንዘ ትሔሱ 'while she lies' (ሐሰወ, the same verb as the false witnesses above; the form ትሔሱ is read as its imperfect, 3fs (?)). Allusion: Proverbs 30:20, where the adulteress 'eats, wipes her mouth, and says, I have done no wrong'; the Geʿez adapts this to washing. The unit ends at ፨.

sentences.t: ወአሜሃ ፡ ብእሲተ ፡ በላዖን ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ባቢሎን ፡ ፀንሰት ፡ ወወለደት ፡ አምሳለ ፡ ንስር ፡ ዘአልቦ ፡ ክንፈ ፡ ኵለንታሁ ፡ ዖፍ ፡ ፍጹም ፤
sentences.l: And-then wife-of Belaon king-of Babylon she-conceived and-she-bore likeness-of eagle which-not-with-him wing, all-of-him bird perfect;
sentences.i: At that time the wife of Belaon, king of Babylon, conceived and bore the likeness of an eagle, without wings, wholly a bird, complete;
sentences.n: ወአሜሃ 'and at that time' (አሜሃ). ብእሲተ በላዖን ንጉሠ ባቢሎን is a three-link construct chain, 'wife-of Belaon king-of Babylon'. ወለደት is a 3fs perfect with the object አምሳለ ንስር 'likeness-of eagle' (አምሳል 'likeness'). ዘአልቦ ክንፈ: አልቦ means 'there is not to him', so ዘአልቦ is 'which has not / without', and ክንፈ is the accusative of ክንፍ 'wing'. ኵለንታሁ 'all of him, his whole self' (ኵለንታ + -ሁ); ዖፍ 'bird'; ፍጹም 'perfect, complete'. The queen's child, then, was a wingless bird-like creature (?), perfect in body as a bird. The phrase ዘአልቦ appears often; I will gloss it 'without' from here.

sentences.t: ወጸውዐታ ፡ ለአመታ ፡ እንተ ፡ ኀርየት ፡ ወፈነወቶ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ምቅላደ ፡ መሶብ ፡ ወአዘዘታ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ያእምር ፡ ፩ ፡ ትገሮ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ባሕር ።
sentences.l: And-she-summoned-her to-her-maid who she-had-chosen, and-she-sent-it into closed-container (?)-of basket, and-she-commanded-her without he-knows one she-might-throw-it into sea.
sentences.i: She summoned her maid, whom she had chosen, and sent the child in a closed (?) basket, and commanded her to throw it into the sea without anyone knowing.
sentences.n: ወጸውዐታ 'and she called her' (ጸውዐ + -ኣ) with ለአመታ 'her maid' (አመት 'handmaid' + -ሃ 'her', ለ- marking the object). እንተ ኀርየት 'whom she had chosen' (feminine relative እንተ + 3fs perfect of ኀረየ). ወፈነወቶ 'and she sent it' (ፈነወ + -ኦ, written -ቶ after a feminine verb). ምቅላደ is unclear (?): perhaps a word for a closure, lid or lock (from ቀለደ?), so 'a closed/locked basket'. መሶብ is a basket (a woven container, in Ethiopia also a serving basket). ወአዘዘታ 'and she commanded her' (አዘዘ 'command' + -ኣ). ዘእንበለ ያእምር ፩ 'without one knowing': ዘእንበለ 'without' with the subjunctive, ፩ the numeral 'one' used as 'anyone'. ትገሮ 'she throw it' I take as a short form or slip for ትውግሮ, which appears two units on (ወገረ 'throw, cast stones') (?); the subjunctive after the command means 'that she throw it'.

sentences.t: ወይእቲኒ ፡ ብእሲተ ፡ ነጋዲ ፡ በጽሐ ፡ ወሊዶታ ፡ ወወለደት ፡ ሕፃነ ፡ ተባዕተ ፡ መምሕረ ፡ ዘሠናይ ፡ ላሕዩ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-also wife-of merchant it-reached her-bearing, and-she-bore child male teacher (?) which good his-appearance;
sentences.i: And the merchant's wife also came to her time, and bore a male child, a 'teacher' (?), fine in appearance;
sentences.n: ወይእቲኒ 'and she too' (ይእቲ + the enclitic -ኒ 'also'). በጽሐ ወሊዶታ: በጽሐ is 3ms 'it reached' (it does not agree with the feminine ብእሲተ ነጋዲ), ወሊዶታ 'her bearing' (the infinitive ወሊዶት + -ኣ 'her', as ጠይቆቶ above is ጠይቆት + -ኦ), so 'her time of delivery arrived' (?); the construction is odd. ወወለደት ሕፃነ ተባዕተ 'and she bore a child, a male' (ተባዕት 'male'). መምሕረ is the accusative of መምሕር 'teacher'; it does not fit the sentence and may be a corruption (?): I give 'a teacher (?)' rather than drop it. ዘሠናይ ላሕዩ 'which good his appearance' = 'fine in appearance', the same phrase as above.

sentences.t: ወዘእንበለ ፡ ታጥብዎ ፡ ጸውዐታ ፡ ለአመታ ፡ እንተ ፡ ኀረየት ፡ ወፈነወቶ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቀማጥረ ፡ ሳጥን ፡ ወአዘዘታ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ያእምር ፡ ፩ ፡ ትውግሮ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ባሕር ፤
sentences.l: And-before she-might-suckle-him, she-summoned-her to-her-maid who she-had-chosen, and-she-sent-it into case-of (?) chest, and-she-commanded-her without he-knows one she-might-throw-it into sea;
sentences.i: And before she could nurse him, she summoned her maid, whom she had chosen, and sent him in a chest (?), and commanded her to throw him into the sea without anyone knowing;
sentences.n: ወዘእንበለ ታጥብዎ: ዘእንበለ 'before/without' + the 3fs subjunctive ታጥብዎ, from አጥበወ 'give suck, nurse' + -ኦ 'him' (?); I read the clause as 'before she could nurse him'. The rest repeats the pattern of the earlier maid scene (see the note there): እንተ ኀረየት, ወፈነወቶ, ወአዘዘታ, ዘእንበለ ያእምር ፩. ቀማጥረ ሳጥን is unclear (?): ሳጥን is 'chest, box'; ቀማጥረ I cannot identify and render with 'case-of' only as a guess. ትውግሮ 'she throw him' (ወገረ, 3fs subjunctive + -ኦ). Notice how closely the two women's actions are paired in the narrative: each calls the maid she chose, with the same instruction.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ፈርሀት ፡ ብእሴሃ ።
sentences.l: For she-feared her-husband.
sentences.i: For she feared her husband.
sentences.n: ፈርሀት 'she feared' (ፈርሀ, 3fs perfect); ብእሴሃ 'her husband' (ብእሲ + -ሃ 'her'), here the object with no preposition. A very short unit that gives the merchant's wife's motive: her fear of her husband is given as the reason (his return, presumably (?)).

sentences.t: ወበአሐቲ ፡ ሌሊት ፡ ወለዳ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ብእሲተ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወበአፈ ፡ ጽባሕ ፡ ፈነዋ ፡ አእማቲሆን ፡ ከመ ፡ ይውግራሆሙ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ባሕር ፡ ለደቂቆን ።
sentences.l: And-in-one night they-bore with wife-of king, and-at-mouth-of morning they-sent their-maids that they-throw-them into sea, to-their-sons.
sentences.i: In a single night the two women bore their children, and at daybreak they sent their maids to throw their children into the sea.
sentences.n: The verb here, and in several below, is the 3rd-feminine-plural perfect, whose ending is -ኣ (ወለዳ 'they (f.) bore', ፈነዋ 'they (f.) sent'); in the plural masculine it would be -ዉ. So ወለዳ ምስለ ብእሲተ ንጉሥ is 'they bore, with the king's wife', that is the merchant's wife and the king's wife together (this broadens the form's earlier gloss). ወበአፈ ጽባሕ 'and at the mouth of morning' = 'at daybreak' (አፍ 'mouth', construct አፈ). Here ፈነዋ is the 3fp perfect 'they (f.) sent', the two mothers being the subject, and አእማቲሆን 'their maids' (plural of አመት + -ሆን) the object, as in l. ከመ ይውግራሆሙ is 'that they cast them' (3fp subjunctive ይውግራ + -ሆሙ); ለደቂቆን 'their sons' (ለ- marking the object + ደቂቅ + -ሆን 'their (f.)'). ደቂቆን uses the shortened -ን for the feminine possessive.

sentences.t: ወበፈቃደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ተራከባ ፡ እላ ፡ አእማት ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ይውግራሆሙ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ባሕር ፡ ወተናገራ ፡ በበይናቲሆን ፡ ወሐተተታ ፡ አመተ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ለአመተ ፡ ነጋዲ ፡ ወትቤላ ፡ ምንት ፡ ዘውስተ ፡ ሣጹንኪ ፤
sentences.l: And-by-will-of God they-met these maids without they-throw-them into sea, and-they-spoke among-themselves (?), and-she-questioned-her maid-of king to-maid-of merchant, and-she-said-to-her, What that-in your-chest;
sentences.i: By God's will these maids met before they threw the children into the sea, and they talked together, and the king's maid questioned the merchant's maid and said to her, 'What is in your chest?'
sentences.n: ወበፈቃደ እግዚኣብሔር 'and by the will of God': በ- + ፈቃድ in the construct state (ፈቃደ), followed by 'God'; the narrator's way of marking providence. ተራከባ 'they (f.) met' (ተራከበ, 3fp perfect; see the ending noted above). ዘእንበለ ይውግራሆሙ 'before they throw them' (ዘእንበለ + subjunctive, as before). ወተናገራ 'and they spoke' (ተናገረ 'converse'); በበይናቲሆን 'among themselves' (?). ወሐተተታ 'and she questioned her' (ሐተተ, 3fs perfect -ት + object suffix -ኣ 'her', doubled by ለአመተ ነጋዲ). አመተ ንጉሥ 'maid-of king' (construct chain), ለአመተ ነጋዲ 'to the maid-of the merchant'. ወትቤላ 'and she said to her' (3fs of ይቤ with the suffix -ላ 'to her'); speakers alternate in the following units, marked each time by ወትቤላ. ምንት ዘውስተ ሣጹንኪ: ምንት 'what?', ዘውስተ 'that (is) in', ሣጹን 'chest' (ሣጹን + -ኪ 'your', feminine addressee). The chest is the container of the merchant's wife's child.

sentences.t: ወአርአየታ ፡ ሕፃነ ፡ ሠናየ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-showed-her child good;
sentences.i: And she showed her a handsome child;
sentences.n: ወአርአየታ 'and she showed her': አርአየ is the causative of ርእየ 'see', so 'cause to see, show', + -ኣ 'her'. ሕፃነ ሠናየ 'a child, good' (both accusative; ሠናይ takes the -ኧ ending, ሠናየ, in agreement).

sentences.t: ወትቤላ ፡ ለምንት ፡ አምጻእኪዮ ፡ ዝየ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-said-to-her, Why you-brought-him here;
sentences.i: And she said to her, 'Why have you brought him here?'
sentences.n: ለምንት 'why?' (ለ- + ምንት 'what'). አምጻእኪዮ 'you (f.) brought him': the causative of መጽአ 'come', so 'bring', 2fs perfect (ending -ኪ) + -ዮ 'him'. ዝየ 'here'. The king's maid asks why the baby has been brought here (presumably to where the children are to be thrown into the sea (?)).

sentences.t: ወትቤላ ፡ እስመ ፡ ብእሲተ ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ ስሕተት ፡ በኀበ ፡ ፩ ፡ እስራኤላዊ ፡ ወፀንሰት ፡ ወወለደት ፡ ወልደ ፡ ወአዘዘተኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እውግሮ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ባሕር ፤
sentences.l: And-she-said-to-her, Because wife-of my-lord error (?) with one Israelite, and-she-conceived and-she-bore son, and-she-commanded-me that-I-throw-him into sea;
sentences.i: She said to her, 'Because my master's wife went astray (?) with an Israelite, and conceived and bore a son, and she commanded me to throw him into the sea.'
sentences.n: The maid reports the facts truthfully. እስመ 'because'. ብእሲተ እግዚእየ 'wife-of my-lord' (እግዚእ 'lord' + -የ 'my'): the merchant is meant. ስሕተት, a noun 'error' in the glossaries, is here a predicate 'went astray' (?), a short form where the earlier verb was ተስሕተት. በኀበ ፩ እስራኤላዊ 'with one Israelite' (ኀበ 'at the side of'; ፩ = 'a certain'; እስራኤላዊ is 'Israelite', from እስራኤል + -ዊ). ወልደ 'a son' (accusative). አዘዘተኒ 'she commanded me': አዘዘት + -ኒ 'me'. ከመ እውግሮ 'that I throw him' (1cs subjunctive of ወገረ + -ኦ).

sentences.t: ወትቤላ ፡ አመተ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ለምንት ፡ ኢያልሀቀት ፡ ዘመጠነዝ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ሕፃነ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-said-to-her, maid-of king, Why not she-brought-up one-of-such good child;
sentences.i: The king's maid said to her, 'Why did she not raise so handsome a child?'
sentences.n: ለምንት ኢያልሀቀት 'why did she not bring up?': ኢ- 'not' + the 3fs ʾa-stem of ልህቀ ('make grow'), the same verb as above. ዘመጠነዝ ሠናይ ሕፃነ: ዘ + መጠነ 'measure' + the demonstrative -ዝ 'this', so 'of this measure', 'such, so great'; the whole is 'a child so good'. Here the king's maid speaks again.

sentences.t: ወትቤላ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ፅንስት ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ኀደጋ ፡ ብእሲሃ ፡ ወወለደት ፡ ወአልሀቀት ፡ ወዝንቱ ፡ በአይቴ ፡ ተሐፅን ፡ ዘባዕድ ፡ ነኪር ፡ ዘርእ ።
sentences.l: And-she-said-to-her, While pregnant she her-husband he-left-her, and-she-bore and-she-brought-up, and-this-one in-what is-nursed (?), of-another strange seed.
sentences.i: She said to her, 'While she was pregnant her husband left her, and she bore and raised the first; and this one, where could he be nursed (?), of another's, of strange seed?'
sentences.n: The merchant's maid answers by repeating the facts of the earlier unit, እንዘ ፅንስት ይእቲ ኀደጋ ብእሲሃ ወወለደት ወአልሀቀት, nearly word for word. The new final clause is hard (?). በአይቴ 'in what / where' (በ- + አይቴ); ተሐፅን I take as a tä-stem of ሐፀነ 'nurse, embrace', 'be nursed', but its person and tense are uncertain (?): it is not a clean 3ms perfect (ተሐፅነ), though the subject ዝንቱ is masculine. ዘባዕድ ነኪር ዘርእ 'of another, strange, seed': ባዕድ 'other', ነኪር 'foreign, strange', ዘርእ 'seed' (the construct is ዘርአ, but here an absolute). The sense seems to be that the child cannot be kept, being another man's seed. Read this clause as uncertain (?).

sentences.t: ወይእቲኒ ፡ ሐተተታ ፡ ወትቤላ ፡ ምንት ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ዘውስተ ፡ መሶብ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-also she-questioned-her and-she-said-to-her, What it that-in basket;
sentences.i: And she in turn asked, 'What is in the basket?'
sentences.n: The merchant's maid now asks about the queen's basket. ወይእቲኒ 'and she too' (as above). ምንት ውእቱ ዘውስተ መሶብ: ምንት 'what', ውእቱ 'it is' (the pronoun serving as copula), ዘውስተ 'that (is) in'; መሶብ 'basket' without a suffix, the same container named earlier.

sentences.t: ወትቤላ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ እግዝእትየ ፡ ወለደት ፡ ዘአልቦ ፡ አርአያ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ላዕሌሁ ፡ አላ ፡ ይመስል ፡ ንስረ ፡ ዘአልቦ ፡ ክንፈ ፡ ወአዘዘተኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እውግሮ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ባሕር ፤
sentences.l: And-she-said-to-her, This my-lady she-bore, which-not-with-him likeness-of man upon-him, but he-resembles eagle which-not-with-him wing, and-she-commanded-me that-I-throw-him into sea;
sentences.i: She said to her, 'This is what my lady bore, one with no human likeness on him, but he looks like an eagle without wings; and she commanded me to throw him into the sea.'
sentences.n: ዘንተ is the accusative of ዝንቱ 'this'; the sentence is 'this my lady bore' (ወለደት 3fs perfect; እግዝእትየ 'my lady', እግዝእት + -የ). ዘአልቦ አርአያ ሰብእ ላዕሌሁ 'which has not the likeness of man upon him': ዘአልቦ 'without', አርአያ 'appearance, likeness', ሰብእ 'man, human being', ላዕሌሁ 'upon him' (ላዕለ + -ሁ). አላ 'but, rather'. ይመስል ንስረ 'he resembles an eagle' (መሰለ, 3ms imperfect, takes the accusative). ዘአልቦ ክንፈ again as above, and ወአዘዘተኒ ከመ እውግሮ ውስተ ባሕር repeats the earlier maid's words. This unit repeats those two earlier phrases verbatim, a feature of the narrative's repeated formulae.

sentences.t: ወይእዜኒ ፡ ሀብንዮ ፡ ለዝንቱ ፡ ወልድኪ ፡ ከመ ፡ እሰዶ ፡ ኀበ ፡ እግዝእትየ ፡ ወአንቲኒ ፡ ንሥኢ ፡ ውግርዮ ፡ ለዝንቱ ፡ ዖፍ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ባሕር ፤
sentences.l: And-now give-me-him to-this your-son, that-I-take-away-him to my-lady, and-you-also take, cast-him to-this bird into sea;
sentences.i: 'And now give me this son of yours, that I may take him to my lady; and you, take this bird and cast it into the sea.'
sentences.n: The proposal of the swap. ሀብንዮ is the imperative 2fs of ወሀበ 'give' + -ኒ 'to me' + -ዮ 'him', so 'give me him'; ለዝንቱ ወልድኪ then repeats the object: 'this, your son' (ወልድኪ = ወልድ + -ኪ 'your (f.)'). ከመ እሰዶ 'that I take him away' (1cs subjunctive + -ኦ; probably ወሰደ 'take, carry off', as ወወሰደት two units on, with its ወ dropped as in ትገሮ for ትውግሮ above, though ሰደ 'drive away' is the other possibility (?)). ወአንቲኒ 'and you too' (አንቲ 'you (f.)' + -ኒ). ንሥኢ 'take!' (ነሥአ, imperative 2fs) and ውግርዮ 'throw him!' (ወገረ, imperative 2fs + -ዮ), both singular feminine commands, to the merchant's maid. ዝንቱ ዖፍ 'this bird': the queen's wingless child is spoken of as 'bird'.

sentences.t: ወገብራ ፡ ከማሁ ።
sentences.l: And-they-did likewise.
sentences.i: And the two did the same.
sentences.n: ወገብራ 'and they (f.) did': ገብረ 'do, make' in the 3fp perfect (the 3fp ending -ኣ, noted at the unit beginning 'And in one night'). ከማሁ 'likewise' (ከመ 'like' + -hu 'him / it'). The swap is done in one short clause; the narrator does not dwell on it.

sentences.t: ወወሰደት ፡ አመተ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ውእተ ፡ ሕፃነ ፡ ኀበ ፡ እግዝእታ ፡ ወተፈሥሐት ፡ ንግሥት ፤
sentences.l: And-she-took maid-of king that child to her-lady, and-she-rejoiced queen;
sentences.i: The king's maid took that child to her mistress, and the queen rejoiced;
sentences.n: ወወሰደት 'and she took away' (ወሰደ; here the verb is the common ወሰደ 'take, carry off', 3fs). ውእተ ሕፃነ 'that child' (ውእተ is the accusative of ውእቱ 'that'). ኀበ እግዝእታ 'to her lady' (ኀበ 'to'; እግዝእት + -ሃ 'her'). ወተፈሥሐት ንግሥት 'and the queen rejoiced': ተፈሥሐ 'rejoice' (tä-stem), 3fs perfect; ንግሥት 'queen'.

sentences.t: ወአርድእዎ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ ከመ ፡ ወለደት ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ንግሥት ፡ ወልደ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-informed-him to-king that she-bore she queen son;
sentences.i: and they informed the king that the queen had borne a son;
sentences.n: ወአርድእዎ 'and they informed him': አርድአ 'inform, make known' (the sense from memory, not checked (?)), 3mp perfect + -ዎ 'him', the object then repeated by ለንጉሥ (the anticipating ለ- pattern). ከመ 'that' introduces the report (ከመ ወለደት ይእቲ ንግሥት ወልደ 'that she bore, she the queen, a son'). The pronoun ይእቲ is a repeated subject for emphasis.

sentences.t: ወወሀብዎ ፡ ለሐፃንያን ፡ ወልህቀ ፡ በቤተ ፡ ንጉሥ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-gave-him to-nurses, and-he-grew in-house-of king;
sentences.i: and they gave him to nurses, and he grew up in the king's house;
sentences.n: ወወሀብዎ 'and they gave him' (ወሀበ, 3mp perfect + -ዎ 'him'), ለሐፃንያን 'to nurses' (the plural of ሐፃኒ, here masculine-plural form). ወልህቀ 'and he grew' (ልህቀ, the G-stem of the verb whose ʾa-stem 'bring up' occurred above). በቤተ ንጉሥ 'in the house-of king': በ- + the construct ቤተ.

sentences.t: ወሰመየቶ ፡ ስሞ ፡ ናቡክድናጸር ፡ በገደ ፡ ዖፍ ፡ ብሂል ፨
sentences.l: And-she-named-him his-name Nebuchadnezzar, in-ገደ bird saying (?);
sentences.i: and she named him, by name Nebuchadnezzar, which means something like 'bird' (?);
sentences.n: ወሰመየቶ 'and she named him' (ሰመየ 'name', 3fs perfect + -ኦ 'him', written -ቶ). ስሞ 'his name' (ስም + the object-case -o), an apposition: 'named him — his name (was) Nebuchadnezzar'. ናቡክድናጸር is the Geʿez spelling of Nebuchadnezzar (the Babylonian king of 2 Kings 24-25 and Daniel). በገደ ዖፍ ብሂል: ብሂል is 'saying, meaning' (a verbal noun of ብህለ 'say'), so 'a saying/meaning of …'. ገደ I cannot identify (?): it may be a corrupt or foreign word, and ዖፍ is 'bird'. The point of the explanation seems to be a folk-etymology linking the name to the bird-child, but I cannot reconstruct it; read this as a gloss of the name, not as certain.

sentences.t: ወበእንተዝ ፡ ተዐውቀ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ በቢሎን ።
sentences.l: And-on-account-of-this it-was-known that seed-of Shem he king-of Babylon.
sentences.i: For this reason it is known that the king of Babylon is of the seed of Shem.
sentences.n: ወበእንተዝ 'and on account of this' (በእንተ + the demonstrative -ዝ). ተዐውቀ is the passive 'it was known' (the tä-stem of ዐወቀ 'know') (?). ዘርአ ሴም 'seed-of Shem': the construct state, and Shem is the son of Noah from whom the Semites, so the Israelites, are said to descend (Genesis 10-11). Since the child is in truth Karmin's, an Israelite's, Nebuchadnezzar would be of Shem's line, which the chronicle uses to claim a Semitic ancestry for the Babylonian king. ንጉሠ በቢሎን: the spelling በቢሎን for Babylon differs from ባቢሎን elsewhere (a variant spelling or slip).

sentences.t: ወመጽአ ፡ ወነሠታ ፡ ለኢየሩሳሌም ፡ በፈቃደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወፄወዎሙ ፡ ለደቂቀ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወአግዐዞሙ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ባቢሎን ፡ ምስለ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ ደቂቁ ፡ ለምናሴ ።
sentences.l: And-he-came and-he-took-her to-Jerusalem by-will-of God, and-he-took-captive-them to-sons-of Israel, and-he-led-them-away to city-of Babylon with sons-of sons-of-him to-Manasseh.
sentences.i: He came and took Jerusalem by the will of God, and took the sons of Israel captive, and led them away to the city of Babylon, with the grandsons of Manasseh.
sentences.n: ወመጽአ 'and he came'. ወነሠታ ለኢየሩሳሌም 'and he seized it, Jerusalem': ነሠተ I take as 'seize, take (a city)' (it may rather mean 'lay bare, demolish') (?), with -ኣ 'it' repeated by ለኢየሩሳሌም, the same object-doubling as before. Allusion: the capture and deportation of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar, 2 Kings 24-25, 2 Chronicles 36; the chronicle presents it as God's will, as the Bible does (e.g. Jeremiah 25). ወፄወዎሙ 'and he took them captive' (ፄወወ, 3ms + -ዎሙ). ወአግዐዞሙ 'and he made them go out, led them off' (the causative of ግዕዘ; sense 'deport' from the context (?)). ሀገረ ባቢሎን 'city-of Babylon' (construct). ደቂቀ እስራኤል 'sons-of Israel' = the Israelites. ምስለ ደቂቀ ደቂቁ ለምናሴ: ደቂቅ is repeated, 'sons-of sons-of-him', and ለምናሴ gives the owner, 'of Manasseh'; so 'with Manasseh's grandsons' (?), the exact relation being loose. The chronicle compresses the history: Manasseh was himself taken to Babylon in 2 Chronicles 33:11.

sentences.t: ወኮነ ፡ ባዕለ ፡ ጥቀ ፡ እስከ ፡ ያቀውም ፡ ሐውልተ ፡ ወርቅ ፡ በሐቅለ ፡ ባቢሎን ፡ ዘ፷ ፡ እመት ፡ ኑኁ ፡ ወ፮ ፡ እመት ፡ ግድሙ ።
sentences.l: And-he-became rich exceedingly, until he-set-up statue-of gold in-plain-of Babylon which-of-60 cubit its-height and-6 cubit its-breadth.
sentences.i: He became exceedingly rich, until he set up a golden statue in the plain of Babylon, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide.
sentences.n: Allusion: the golden image of Daniel 3:1, 'whose height was sixty cubits and its breadth six cubits', set up in the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon. ወኮነ 'and he became' (ኮነ, 'be, become'). ባዕለ is the accusative of ባዕል 'owner, rich man', and ጥቀ 'exceedingly', so 'very rich', though the context makes 'powerful' also possible. እስከ ያቀውም 'until he sets up' (እስከ + the 3ms subjunctive of አቀመ). ሐውልተ ወርቅ 'statue-of gold' is a construct chain. In the source ዘ፷ is written as one word: the relative ዘ 'which (is)' fused to the numeral ፷ (60), and ወ፮ is ወ 'and' fused to ፮ (6); both are as printed and I leave them so. Numerals: ፷ is 60 and ፮ is 6; the spoken forms are from memory (?): ስሳ (səssa) for 60 and, for 6, the masculine ስድስቱ (sədsətu) with a feminine ስድስ before the feminine እመት (?), as the house entry for ፫ has ሠለስ (?); the plain reading is 'of sixty cubits'. እመት 'cubit'; ኑኁ 'its height' and ግድሙ 'its breadth' (each a noun + -u 'its'). በሐቅለ ባቢሎን 'in the plain-of Babylon' (ሐቅል 'field, plain').

sentences.t: ወኮነ ፡ ዕቡየ ፡ ልብ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ኣሠርቅ ፡ ፀሐየ ፡ በላዕለ ፡ ሰማይ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-became proud-one heart, and-he-said, I-will-cause-to-rise sun above heaven;
sentences.i: He grew proud of heart, and said, 'I will make the sun rise above heaven';
sentences.n: ወኮነ ዕቡየ ልብ 'and he became proud, of heart': ዕቡይ 'proud', the accusative ዕቡየ as predicate, with ልብ 'heart' as a genitive-like noun ('proud-of heart'). Allusion: the pride of Nebuchadnezzar, Daniel 4 (4:30, 'Is not this great Babylon, which I have built…?'); the boast to set himself above heaven also echoes the king of Babylon in Isaiah 14:13-14 ('I will ascend above the heights of the clouds'). ኣሠርቅ is the 1cs imperfect of the causative ʾa-stem of ሠረቀ 'rise (of the sun)': 'I will make rise'; the initial ኣ (written with the fourth-order sign) is a variant spelling. ፀሐየ 'sun' (accusative); በላዕለ 'above, over'.

sentences.t: ወሰገደ ፡ ለጣዖት ።
sentences.l: And-he-bowed-down to-idol.
sentences.i: and he bowed down to an idol.
sentences.n: ወሰገደ 'and he bowed down' (ሰገደ, 3ms perfect); ለጣዖት 'to the idol (or idols)' (ጣዖት, said to be a Greek loan-word (?), and ለ- 'to' marks the one worshipped). Compare Daniel 3, where the image is set up for worship.

sentences.t: ወሠረዎ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ያእምር ፡ ኪያሁ ፡ ወመክፈልቶሂ ፡ ምስለ ፡ አራዊተ ፡ ገዳም ፡ ረሰየ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-drove-out-him God so-that he-might-know him, and-his-portion-also with beasts-of wilderness He-appointed;
sentences.i: And God drove him out, that he might know Him, and appointed his portion also with the beasts of the wilderness;
sentences.n: Allusion: Daniel 4:25, 32, where Nebuchadnezzar is driven from men and 'your dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field' until he knows that the Most High rules; he lives in the wild seven times (the chronicle says years, below). ወሠረዎ 'and he drove him out' (ሠረወ 'drive away, remove' (?), 3ms + -ኦ). ከመ ያእምር ኪያሁ 'that he might know him', with the independent object pronoun ኪያሁ, 'him': God, from the next unit. ወመክፈልቶሂ 'and his portion, too' (መክፈልት 'portion, share' + -ሁ 'his' + the enclitic -ሂ 'also, even'). ምስለ አራዊተ ገዳም 'with beasts-of wilderness' (the plural አራዊት in the construct). ረሰየ 'He made, appointed' (3ms perfect), the object coming first.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ አእመረ ፡ ስመ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ ዓመት ፡ ፯ ፡ ምሕሮ ፡ ወአግብኦ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ንስሓ ፤
sentences.l: And-when he-knew name-of God, after year 7, He-had-mercy-on-him and-He-brought-him-back into repentance;
sentences.i: And when he came to know the name of God, after seven years, He took pity on him and brought him back to repentance;
sentences.n: Allusion: Daniel 4:34-37, where his reason returns and he blesses the Most High. ወሶበ 'and when'; አእመረ 'he knew' (the ʾa-stem used as a simple verb, 'know, recognise'); ስመ እግዚኣብሔር 'name-of God'. እምድኅረ 'after' (እም- + ድኅረ 'behind'). ዓመት ፯ 'year 7', the numeral ፯ (7; spoken form from memory (?): ሰብዐቱ säbʿatu, or a feminine ሰብዐ before the feminine ዓመት) placed after its noun, which by the house entry for ፫ can also be the ordinal ('the seventh year', ሳብዕ (?)); I keep 'seven years', as the Bible says 'seven times' (Daniel 4:25). ምሕሮ 'He had mercy on him' (ምሐረ + -ኦ; the text has 6th-order ሕ, where the perfect + suffix would be ምሐሮ, so a spelling slip, or an imperative form read as narrative (?)), and ወአግብኦ 'and He brought him back' (the causative of ገብአ 'return', + -ኦ). ንስሓ 'repentance'.

sentences.t: ወኮነት ፡ መንግሥተ ፡ ባቢሎን ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ዘለዘርኡ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-it-became kingdom-of Babylon to-him, which-for-his-seed, until for-ever. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: And the kingdom of Babylon became his, and his offspring's, for ever.
sentences.n: ወኮነት 'and it became' (the feminine of ኮነ, because መንግሥተ 'kingdom' is feminine); መንግሥተ ባቢሎን 'kingdom-of Babylon' (construct). ሎቱ 'to him' (ለ + -ቱ), then ዘለዘርኡ 'which (is) to his seed' (ዘ- + ለ- + ዘርእ + -u): 'and to his offspring'. እስከ ለዓለም 'until for ever' (ዓለም 'age, world, eternity'). The chapter closes with the run of six ፨ signs; they are the end-mark of the edition (I take it to be a scribal close (?)) and have no translation.
